Subject: sudden p99 jump on vectors endpoint after this morning's update

Hi Michael,

We're seeing a sudden regression on the vectors endpoint used by our search ranker. Baseline p95 ~120ms / p99 ~250ms; starting ~08:30 UTC this morning p95 jumped to ~420ms and p99 to ~880ms. That's across multiple regions but most visible in us-west. We attached a CSV with traces and a short screenshot of our dashboard.

Traffic hasn't materially increased on our side. We rolled a quick config check and nothing obvious. Your status page shows a catalog patch around 08:15 UTC (catalog v2.14). Can you confirm if anything in that patch could affect latency for short-sequence embeddings? This spike is impacting search latency in production and causing user-facing degradation.

Attachments: orion_p99_trace_20261113.csv, timeline-screenshot.png

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: FW: sudden p99 jump on vectors endpoint after this morning's update

Quick summary of findings from the initial triage:
- Observed spike in p95/p99 for sequences <=64 starting at 08:22 UTC, coincident with catalog v2.14 rollout.
- Catalog patch added two new model variants: v-catalog/vec-lite-q8 and v-catalog/vec-lite-q4 (quantized lower-precision variants) and updated the routing policy to include auto-fallback to the "low-cost" family for capacity reasons.
- For short sequences our kernel selector is incorrectly preferring the q4 path on A100-p4d nodes for certain batch size distributions. That path triggers a slower kernel due to an unexpected kernel switch and cross-stream synchronization (we're seeing frequent device context switches). In production traces this shows up as a ~2.5–3x tail amplification for p99.
- Additionally, the new routing policy increases mixing of traffic across device pools which prevented the usual batching aggregation; tiny batches (1–3) were dispatched more often, increasing wakeup overhead.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Rollback catalog v2.14 to v2.13 (fast, ~6–8 minutes, risk: briefly sync/routing churn).
2) Update routing policy to exclude q4 variants for low-latency routes (safe, takes ~20 minutes to propagate).
3) Canary a modified kernel selection tweak that forces prefer-low-latency kernels for seq<=64 (requires build, ~4–6 hours).

Recommendation: rollback to v2.13 immediately to stop user impact, then revert routing policy to prevent auto-fallback to q4 variants; afterwards, schedule a controlled re-introduction with canary and A/B to validate tail behavior. I'm prepping the rollback plan now.

Logs referenced: kernel-choice.log, scheduling-traces-0815-0830.log (attached to internal ticket).

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Expected interruption: < 10 minutes during routing sync. We will monitor p95/p99 closely and provide a live update in this thread at +5/+15 minutes after the rollback window.

We will also provide a postmortem and remediation timeline (including canary and kernel selection fix). As a gesture for the disruption, we'll apply a one-month service credit to your account — I'll confirm the exact credit in the follow-up.

If 11:00 UTC conflicts with high-traffic operations on your side, please let us know now and we can move the rollback earlier/later within the next hour.

Best,
